title: Evals: quality root-cause capture (scratchpad) — May 5 2026
content:
Context:
- Quick prep for the weekly optimize/evals sync (30 min). This is my scratchpad for distilling the recent quality regression signal on the /chat/generate route for the commerce assistant workload.
- High level: since 2026-04-28 we've seen a 6–9% drop in 'useful_response' metric on canary traffic; surfaced by anomaly alert (metrics pipeline).

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick signal recap & priority (5 min)
2) Hypothesis triage (10 min)
3) Experiment ideas + A/B plan (10 min)
4) Immediate actions + owners (5 min)

Key signal details (brief):
- Metric: "useful_response" (binary automated eval tied to rubric set commerce_v2)
- Scope: canary traffic (10% of production), model variant: redwood-3b-quant-v2
- Onset: 2026-04-28 03:00 UTC; peaked 2026-04-29
- Magnitude: relative drop 6–9% absolute depending on slice
- Which slices worse: multi-turn > single-turn, prompts with long system messages, heavy entity-rewrite cases (SKU normalization)
- Related: token-costs stable, latency unchanged => suggests model output quality change vs infra issue

Hypotheses (ranked, initial):
A) Model variant regression: new build of redwood-3b-quant-v2 has altered sampling/temperature default or postprocessing step changed (high prior).
B) Prompt-set drift: a recent prompt set tweak (PR#4821) introduced a system message phrasing that reduces grounding in product catalog.
C) Serving compilation/kernel change: a kernel scheduling tweak rolled to canary that affects fp16 numerics in some attention patterns (less likely; latency stable).
D) Data-dependent eval flakiness: eval harness has a gap for certain SKU formats introduced by upstream dataset normalization change (possible).

Quick evidence matrix (notes):
- PR#4821 (linked): small prompt tweak merged 2026-04-27 — timing aligns with onset.
- Canary config: rollout of new runtime image 2026-04-26 — verify exact flags (Diego to confirm).
- Regression repro locally: I ran 50 sample traces from canary on baseline model (redwood-3b-quant-v1) vs v2; preliminary manual review shows v2 more likely to drop out of entity mention (7/50 vs 14/50) but need larger N.

Immediate experiment ideas (fast, cheap):
1) A/B shadow: route 1000 recent failing traces through both v1 & v2 (offline) and compute useful_response. Owner: Zuri. Est: 4–6 hours.
2) Prompt revert test: temporarily apply pre-PR#4821 system prompt on canary for 24h and observe metric. Owner: Maya. Est: low risk; requires feature-flag toggle.
3) Kernel flag rollback: test canary runtime image with previous kernel flags in staging (Diego + infra). Est: 1 day including perf smoke.
4) Focused eval harness: create a slice filter for SKU-normalization cases (regex-based) and run 5k evals to get stable CI. Owner: Liam. Est: 1 day.

Measurement plan + success criteria:
- Primary metric: useful_response (binary) at day-1 and day-3 for the test slices.
- Secondary: BLEU/ROUGE-lite scores, human spot checks (10 examples per slice).
- Success: recovery to within 1% of pre-regression baseline on canary slices or identification of a root cause with reproducible repro.

Risks/guardrails:
- Prompt revert could mask other regressions — do not escalate to full prod without AB test and manual inspect.
- Kernel rollbacks require infra windows; ensure fallback path documented.

Meeting notes (to capture live):
- Confirmed PR#4821 wording likely candidate — Maya to paste diff to slack thread for quick eyeball.
- Diego: runtime image did have small scheduling change but only for huge-batch paths; not expected for canary sizes. He will run a targeted numeric-stability test.
- Liam: will spin up the SKU-normalization slice in eval harness and return a CSV with per-example results.
- I will run the offline A/B using last 72h failing traces and attach aggregated stats + examples.

Follow-up action items (owner — due):
- Maya: roll a prompt revert to canary via feature-flag, monitor useful_response 24h (due 2026-05-06).
- Diego: run numeric stability kernel test + confirm whether kernel flags differ between images (due 2026-05-06).
- Liam: generate SKU-slice eval results (5k examples) and upload CSV to confluence page RL-2048 (due 2026-05-07).
- Zuri: run offline A/B, produce summarized metrics and 30 manually triaged examples (due 2026-05-06).
- All: quick async review in #optimize-evals slack of top 10 failing examples (target done 2026-05-06).

Open questions / things to capture in follow-up:
- If prompt revert fixes, do we backfill a canary-level AB across traffic to ensure no downstream regressions? (should plan 2-day AB).
- Is there any confounding change in upstream data normalization (SKU canonicalization) around 2026-04-25 to 04-28? Tagging data infra team if needed.
- Human evaluation: who can spare 1–2 hours for spot checks next week? Marking Maya + Rajiv as potential reviewers.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep examples minimal and representative; prefer multi-turn sequences where entity rewriting occurs mid-dialog.
- Save samples into a new folder users/zuri-thompson/evals/samples/ for quick sharing.
- Add small script to reproduce prompt-set application locally (wrap the prompt template + context) and include seed for deterministic sampling.

Raw quick checklist before next sync:
- [ ] Offline A/B run started (Zuri)
- [ ] Prompt revert toggled in canary (Maya)
- [ ] Kernel numeric test (Diego)
- [ ] SKU-slice eval CSV (Liam)
- [ ] Post findings in #optimize-evals and update confluence summary

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and copy salient actions into the team's weekly notes once we have the A/B numbers.
